title.zh: 卷五十三 志第五: 曆二
title.raw: 卷五十三 志第五: 曆二 Volume 53 Treatises 6: Calendar 2

sentences.zh: 曆二 ○授時曆議下交食

translations.literal: Calendar 2 ○ Discussion on Eclipses, Part 2 of the Shoushi Calendar Treatise
translations.idiomatic: Calendar 2 ○ Discussion on Eclipses under the Shoushi Calendar Treatise

sentences.zh: 曆法疏密，驗在交食，然推步之術難得其密，加時有早晚，食分有淺深，取其密合，不容偶然。

translations.literal: Whether a calendrical method is coarse or precise is verified through eclipses; yet the techniques of astronomical calculation are hard to attain precision; the calculated moment may be early or late, and the degree of eclipse may be shallow or deep. To achieve close agreement cannot be left to chance.
translations.idiomatic: The precision of a calendar is tested by eclipses, yet astronomical calculation is difficult to make exact: the predicted moment may come too early or too late, and the eclipse may be partial or total. A close match cannot be achieved by chance alone.

sentences.zh: 推演加時，必本於躔離朓朒；

translations.literal: To compute the calculated moment, one must rely on the positions of celestial bodies and the waxing and waning of the moon;
translations.idiomatic: Computing the moment of an eclipse must rest on the positions of the heavenly bodies and the phases of the moon;

sentences.zh: 考求食分，必本於距交遠近；

translations.literal: To determine the degree of eclipse, one must rely on the distance from the nodal crossing;
translations.idiomatic: Determining the degree of eclipse must rest on how far the conjunction is from the lunar node;

sentences.zh: 茍入氣盈縮、入轉遲疾未得其正，則合朔不失之先，必失之後。

translations.literal: If the entering of qi expansion-contraction and entering of rotation fast-slow are not correctly obtained, then if new moon conjunction is not missed early, it will certainly be missed late.
translations.idiomatic: If the corrections for solar-term variation and the moon's anomalistic motion are not right, then when the new moon is not predicted too early, it will inevitably be predicted too late.

sentences.zh: 合朔失之先後，則虧食時刻，其能密乎？

translations.literal: If new moon conjunction is missed early or late, how can the moment of eclipse be precise?
translations.idiomatic: If the new moon is off in timing, how can the eclipse moment be accurate?

sentences.zh: 日月俱東行，而日遲月疾，月追及日，是為一會。

translations.literal: Both sun and moon move eastward, but the sun is slow and the moon is fast; when the moon catches up to the sun, this constitutes one conjunction.
translations.idiomatic: Sun and moon both travel eastward, but the sun moves slowly and the moon swiftly; when the moon overtakes the sun, that is one conjunction.

sentences.zh: 交值之道，有陽曆陰曆；

translations.literal: As for the path of nodal crossing, there are yang-calendar and yin-calendar;
translations.idiomatic: The nodes have their yang and yin passages;

sentences.zh: 交會之期，有中前中後；

translations.literal: The timing of nodal conjunction has central-before, central, and central-after;
translations.idiomatic: Conjunctions at the nodes may occur before, at, or after the central crossing;

sentences.zh: 加以地形南北東西之不同，人目高下邪直之各異，此食分多寡，理不得一者也。

translations.literal: Adding the differences of terrain north-south and east-west, and the varying heights and angles at which observers see, the degree of eclipse cannot by principle be uniform.
translations.idiomatic: When one further accounts for differences of latitude and longitude, and for whether an observer sees the event high or low, straight on or at an angle, the degree of eclipse cannot by nature be the same everywhere.

sentences.zh: 今合朔既正，則加時無早晚之差；

translations.literal: Now that new moon conjunction is correct, there is no difference of early or late in the calculated moment;
translations.idiomatic: With the new moon correctly determined, the predicted moment shows no early-or-late error;

sentences.zh: 氣刻適中，則食分無強弱之失；

translations.literal: When the qi and ke are properly adjusted, there is no error of strong or weak in the degree of eclipse;
translations.idiomatic: With the solar-term corrections properly applied, the degree of eclipse is no longer too large or too small;

sentences.zh: 推而上之，自《詩》、《書》、《春秋》及三國以來所載虧食，無不合焉者。

translations.literal: Extrapolating upward, all recorded eclipses from the Classic of Poetry, Documents, Spring and Autumn, and since the Three Kingdoms, none fail to accord.
translations.idiomatic: Working backward from the present, every eclipse recorded since the Classic of Poetry, the Documents, the Spring and Autumn Annals, and the Three Kingdoms period agrees with it.

sentences.zh: 合於既往，則行之悠久，自可無弊矣。

translations.literal: If it agrees with the past, then in long practice it can naturally be without flaw.
translations.idiomatic: Agreement with past records assures that long use will be without defect.

sentences.zh: 《詩》、《書》所載日食二事

translations.literal: Two matters of solar eclipse recorded in the Classic of Poetry and Documents
translations.idiomatic: Two solar eclipses recorded in the Classic of Poetry and the Documents

sentences.zh: 《書·胤征》：「惟仲康肇位四海。

translations.literal: Documents, Punitive Expedition of Yin: "When Zhong Kang first took the throne over the four seas.
translations.idiomatic: From the Documents, "Punitive Expedition against Min": "When Zhong Kang first ascended and ruled the four quarters.

sentences.zh: 乃季秋月朔，辰弗集於房。」

translations.literal: Then on the new moon of autumn in the last month, the heavenly bodies did not gather in the House."
translations.idiomatic: On the new moon of the last month of autumn, the stars did not gather in the House constellation."

sentences.zh: 今按《大衍曆》作仲康即位之五年癸巳，距辛巳三千四百八年，九月庚戌朔，泛交二十六日五千四百二十一分入食限。

translations.literal: Now according to the Dayan Calendar, it was the fifth year of Zhong Kang's accession, year guisi; 3,408 years from xinsi; new moon gengxu in the ninth month; general crossing 26 days 5,421 parts entering eclipse limit.
translations.idiomatic: According to the Dayan Calendar, this was the fifth year of Zhong Kang's reign (guisi), 3,408 years after xinsi; on the gengxu new moon of the ninth month, the general nodal distance was 26 days and 5,421 parts within the eclipse limit.

sentences.zh: 《詩·小雅·十月之交》，大夫刺幽王也。

translations.literal: Classic of Poetry, Minor Odes, "The Approaching Fullness of the Tenth Month": a grandee satirizing King You.
translations.idiomatic: From the Classic of Poetry, Minor Odes, "The Fullness of the Tenth Month": a minister's critique of King You of Zhou.

sentences.zh: 「十月之交，朔日辛卯，日有食之，亦孔之醜。」

translations.literal: "At the fullness of the tenth month, on the new moon day xinmao, the sun was eclipsed—how very dreadful."
translations.idiomatic: "At the turning of the tenth month, on the xinmao new moon, the sun was eclipsed—a most terrible omen."

sentences.zh: 今按梁太史令虞絪云：十月辛卯朔，在幽王六年乙丑朔。

translations.literal: Now according to Liang Grand Astrologer Yu Yin: the xinmao new moon of the tenth month falls in the sixth year of King You, year yichou.
translations.idiomatic: According to Yu Yin, Grand Astrologer of Liang, the xinmao new moon of the tenth month occurred in the sixth year of King You (yichou).

sentences.zh: 《大衍》亦以為然。

translations.literal: The Dayan Calendar also holds this to be so.
translations.idiomatic: The Dayan Calendar agrees.

sentences.zh: 以《授時曆》推之，是歲十月辛卯朔，泛交十四日五千七百九分入食限。

translations.literal: Calculated by the Shoushi Calendar, in that year the xinmao new moon of the tenth month had general crossing 14 days 5,709 parts entering eclipse limit.
translations.idiomatic: By the Shoushi Calendar, the xinmao new moon of the tenth month of that year had a general nodal distance of 14 days and 5,709 parts within the eclipse limit.

sentences.zh: 《春秋》日食三十七事隱公三年辛酉歲，春王二月己巳，日有食之。

translations.literal: Thirty-seven solar eclipses in the Spring and Autumn Annals: In the third year of Duke Yin, year xinyou, in the king's second month of spring on jisi, the sun was eclipsed.
translations.idiomatic: Thirty-seven solar eclipses in the Spring and Autumn Annals. In the third year of Duke Yin (xinyou), on jisi in the king's second month of spring, there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 杜預云：「不書朔，史官失之。

translations.literal: Du Yu said: "The new moon is not recorded—the historiographer erred.
translations.idiomatic: Du Yu said: "The new moon was not recorded; the historiographer had made an error.

sentences.zh: 」《公羊》云：「日食或言朔或不言朔，或日或不日，或失之前或失之後，失之前者朔在前也，失之後者朔在後也。

translations.literal: " The Gongyang Commentary says: "For solar eclipses, sometimes the new moon is stated and sometimes not, sometimes the day and sometimes not; sometimes the error is before and sometimes after—if before, the new moon is ahead; if after, the new moon is behind.
translations.idiomatic: " The Gongyang Commentary says: "For solar eclipses, the new moon may or may not be given, the day may or may not be given; the error may lie before or after the event—if before, the new moon was placed too early; if after, too late.

sentences.zh: 」《穀梁》云：「言日不言朔，食晦日也。

translations.literal: " The Guliang Commentary says: "The day is given but not the new moon—the eclipse was on the last day of the month.
translations.idiomatic: " The Guliang Commentary says: "Only the day is given, not the new moon—the eclipse fell on the last day of the month.

sentences.zh: 」姜岌校《春秋》日食云：「是歲二月己亥朔，無己巳，似失一閏。

translations.literal: " Jiang Ji, collating Spring and Autumn eclipses, said: "In that year the jihai new moon of the second month—there is no jisi; it seems an intercalary month was missed.
translations.idiomatic: " Jiang Ji, reviewing Spring and Autumn eclipses, said: "That year the second month's new moon was jihai; there was no jisi day—it appears an intercalary month was omitted.

sentences.zh: 三月己巳朔，去交分入食限。

translations.literal: The jisi new moon of the third month, distance from crossing entering eclipse limit.
translations.idiomatic: The jisi new moon of the third month fell within the eclipse limit by nodal distance.

sentences.zh: 」《大衍》與姜岌合。

translations.literal: " The Dayan Calendar agrees with Jiang Ji.
translations.idiomatic: " The Dayan Calendar agrees with Jiang Ji.

sentences.zh: 今《授時曆》推之，是歲三月己巳朔，加時在晝，去交分二十六日六千六百三十一入食限。

translations.literal: Now calculated by the Shoushi Calendar, in that year the jisi new moon of the third month, calculated moment in daytime, distance from crossing 26 days 6,631 entering eclipse limit.
translations.idiomatic: By the Shoushi Calendar, the jisi new moon of the third month of that year occurred in daylight, with a nodal distance of 26 days and 6,631 parts within the eclipse limit.

sentences.zh: 桓公三年壬申歲，七月壬辰朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: Third year of Duke Huan, year renshen: on the renchen new moon of the seventh month, the sun was eclipsed.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Duke Huan (renshen), on the renchen new moon of the seventh month, there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 姜岌以為是歲七月癸亥朔，無壬辰，亦失閏。

translations.literal: Jiang Ji held that in that year the seventh month had guihai new moon; there was no renchen—again an intercalary month was missed.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Ji held that the seventh month's new moon that year was guihai; there was no renchen day—again an intercalary month had been omitted.

sentences.zh: 其八月壬辰朔，去交分入食限。

translations.literal: Its renchen new moon of the eighth month, distance from crossing entering eclipse limit.
translations.idiomatic: The renchen new moon of the eighth month fell within the eclipse limit by nodal distance.

sentences.zh: 《大衍》與姜岌合。

translations.literal: The Dayan Calendar agrees with Jiang Ji.
translations.idiomatic: The Dayan Calendar agrees with Jiang Ji.

sentences.zh: 以今曆推之，是歲八月壬辰朔，加時在晝，食六分一十四秒。

translations.literal: Calculated by the present calendar, in that year the renchen new moon of the eighth month, calculated moment in daytime, eclipse six parts fourteen seconds.
translations.idiomatic: By the present calendar, the renchen new moon of the eighth month of that year occurred in daylight, with an eclipse of six parts and fourteen seconds.

sentences.zh: 桓公十七年丙戌歲，冬十月朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: Seventeenth year of Duke Huan, year bingxu: on the new moon of the tenth month of winter, the sun was eclipsed.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year of Duke Huan (bingxu), on the new moon of the tenth month of winter, there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 《左氏》云：「不書日，史官失之。

translations.literal: The Zuo Commentary says: "The day is not recorded—the historiographer erred.
translations.idiomatic: The Zuo Commentary says: "The day was not recorded; the historiographer had made an error.

sentences.zh: 」《大衍》推得在十一月交分入食限，失閏也。

translations.literal: " The Dayan Calendar calculates it in the eleventh month with crossing distance entering eclipse limit—an intercalary month was missed.
translations.idiomatic: " The Dayan Calendar places it in the eleventh month within the eclipse limit by nodal distance—an intercalary month had been omitted.

sentences.zh: 以今曆推之，是歲十一月加時在晝，交分二十六日八千五百六十入食限。

translations.literal: Calculated by the present calendar, in that year the eleventh month calculated moment in daytime, crossing distance 26 days 8,560 entering eclipse limit.
translations.idiomatic: By the present calendar, the eleventh month of that year had a daylight eclipse, with a nodal distance of 26 days and 8,560 parts within the eclipse limit.

sentences.zh: 莊公十八年乙巳歲，春王三月，日有食之。

translations.literal: Eighteenth year of Duke Zhuang, year yisi: in the king's third month of spring, the sun was eclipsed.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year of Duke Zhuang (yisi), in the king's third month of spring, there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 《穀梁》云：「不言日，不言朔，夜食也。

translations.literal: The Guliang Commentary says: "Neither day nor new moon is stated—it was a night eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: The Guliang Commentary says: "Neither the day nor the new moon is given—it was a nighttime eclipse.

sentences.zh: 」《大衍》推是歲五月朔，交分入食限，三月不應食。

translations.literal: " The Dayan Calendar calculates the fifth month new moon of that year with crossing distance entering eclipse limit; the third month should not have had an eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: " The Dayan Calendar places the eclipse at the fifth month's new moon of that year within the eclipse limit; the third month should not have had one.

sentences.zh: 以今曆推之，是歲三月朔，不入食限。

translations.literal: Calculated by the present calendar, in that year the third month new moon does not enter eclipse limit.
translations.idiomatic: By the present calendar, the third month's new moon of that year does not fall within the eclipse limit.

sentences.zh: 五月壬子朔，加時在晝，交分入食限，蓋誤五為三。

translations.literal: The renzi new moon of the fifth month, calculated moment in daytime, crossing distance entering eclipse limit—probably five was mistaken for three.
translations.idiomatic: The renzi new moon of the fifth month occurred in daylight within the eclipse limit—likely "five" was written as "three."

sentences.zh: 莊公二十五年壬子歲，六月辛未朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: Twenty-fifth year of Duke Zhuang, year renzi: on the xinwei new moon of the sixth month, the sun was eclipsed.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fifth year of Duke Zhuang (renzi), on the xinwei new moon of the sixth month, there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 《大衍》推之，七月辛未朔，交分入食限。

translations.literal: The Dayan Calendar calculates it as the xinwei new moon of the seventh month, crossing distance entering eclipse limit.
translations.idiomatic: The Dayan Calendar places it at the xinwei new moon of the seventh month within the eclipse limit.

sentences.zh: 以今曆推之，是歲七月辛未朔，加時在晝，交分二十七日四百八十九入食限，失閏也。

translations.literal: Calculated by the present calendar, in that year the xinwei new moon of the seventh month, calculated moment in daytime, crossing distance 27 days 489 entering eclipse limit—an intercalary month was missed.
translations.idiomatic: By the present calendar, the xinwei new moon of the seventh month of that year occurred in daylight, with a nodal distance of 27 days and 489 parts within the eclipse limit—an intercalary month had been omitted.

sentences.zh: 莊公二十六年癸丑歲，冬十有二月癸亥朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: Twenty-sixth year of Duke Zhuang, year guichou: on the guihai new moon of the twelfth month of winter, the sun was eclipsed.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year of Duke Zhuang (guichou), on the guihai new moon of the twelfth month of winter, there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 今曆推之，是歲十二月癸亥朔，加時在晝，交分十四日三千五百五十一入食限。

translations.literal: Calculated by the present calendar, in that year the guihai new moon of the twelfth month, calculated moment in daytime, crossing distance 14 days 3,551 entering eclipse limit.
translations.idiomatic: By the present calendar, the guihai new moon of the twelfth month of that year occurred in daylight, with a nodal distance of 14 days and 3,551 parts within the eclipse limit.

sentences.zh: 莊公三十年丁巳歲，九月庚午朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: Thirtieth year of Duke Zhuang, year dingsi: on the gengwu new moon of the ninth month, the sun was eclipsed.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirtieth year of Duke Zhuang (dingsi), on the gengwu new moon of the ninth month, there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 今曆推之，是歲十月庚午朔，加時在晝，去交分十四日四千六百九十六入食限，失閏也。

translations.literal: Calculated by the present calendar, in that year the gengwu new moon of the tenth month, calculated moment in daytime, distance from crossing 14 days 4,696 entering eclipse limit—an intercalary month was missed.
translations.idiomatic: By the present calendar, the gengwu new moon of the tenth month of that year occurred in daylight, with a nodal distance of 14 days and 4,696 parts within the eclipse limit—an intercalary month had been omitted.

sentences.zh: 《大衍》同。

translations.literal: The Dayan Calendar agrees.
translations.idiomatic: The Dayan Calendar agrees.

sentences.zh: 僖公十二年癸酉歲，春王三月庚午朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: Twelfth year of Duke Xi, year guiyou: in the king's third month of spring on the gengwu new moon, the sun was eclipsed.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year of Duke Xi (guiyou), on the gengwu new moon of the king's third month of spring, there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 姜氏云：「三月朔，交不應食，在誤條；

translations.literal: Master Jiang said: "The third month new moon—the crossing should not have had an eclipse; it belongs among erroneous entries;
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Ji said: "The third month's new moon should not have had an eclipse by nodal distance; this belongs among erroneous entries;

sentences.zh: 其五月庚午朔，去交分入食限。

translations.literal: Its gengwu new moon of the fifth month, distance from crossing entering eclipse limit.
translations.idiomatic: the gengwu new moon of the fifth month fell within the eclipse limit by nodal distance.

sentences.zh: 」《大衍》同。

translations.literal: " The Dayan Calendar agrees.
translations.idiomatic: " The Dayan Calendar agrees.

sentences.zh: 今曆推之，是歲五月庚午朔，加時在晝，去交分二十六日五千一百九十二入食限，蓋五誤為三。

translations.literal: Calculated by the present calendar, in that year the gengwu new moon of the fifth month, calculated moment in daytime, distance from crossing 26 days 5,192 entering eclipse limit—probably five was mistaken for three.
translations.idiomatic: By the present calendar, the gengwu new moon of the fifth month of that year occurred in daylight, with a nodal distance of 26 days and 5,192 parts within the eclipse limit—likely "five" was written as "three."

sentences.zh: 僖公十五年丙子歲，夏五月，日有食之。

translations.literal: Fifteenth year of Duke Xi, year bingzi: in the fifth month of summer, the sun was eclipsed.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year of Duke Xi (bingzi), in the fifth month of summer, there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 《左氏》云：「不書朔與日，史官失之也。

translations.literal: The Zuo Commentary says: "Neither new moon nor day is recorded—the historiographer erred.
translations.idiomatic: The Zuo Commentary says: "Neither the new moon nor the day was recorded; the historiographer had made an error.

sentences.zh: 」《大衍》推四月癸丑朔，去交分入食限，差一閏。

translations.literal: " The Dayan Calendar calculates the guichou new moon of the fourth month, distance from crossing entering eclipse limit—off by one intercalary month.
translations.idiomatic: " The Dayan Calendar places it at the guichou new moon of the fourth month within the eclipse limit—one intercalary month off.

sentences.zh: 今曆推之，是歲四月癸丑朔，去交分一日一千三百一十六入食限。

translations.literal: Calculated by the present calendar, in that year the guichou new moon of the fourth month, distance from crossing 1 day 1,316 entering eclipse limit.
translations.idiomatic: By the present calendar, the guichou new moon of the fourth month of that year had a nodal distance of 1 day and 1,316 parts within the eclipse limit.

sentences.zh: 文公元年乙未歲，二月癸亥朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: First year of Duke Wen, year yiwei: on the guihai new moon of the second month, the sun was eclipsed.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Duke Wen (yiwei), on the guihai new moon of the second month, there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 姜氏云：「二月甲午朔，無癸亥。

translations.literal: Master Jiang said: "The jiawu new moon of the second month—there is no guihai.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Ji said: "The second month's new moon was jiawu; there was no guihai day.

sentences.zh: 三月癸亥朔，入食限。

translations.literal: The guihai new moon of the third month enters eclipse limit.
translations.idiomatic: The guihai new moon of the third month falls within the eclipse limit.

sentences.zh: 」《大衍》亦以為然。

translations.literal: " The Dayan Calendar also holds this to be so.
translations.idiomatic: " The Dayan Calendar agrees.

sentences.zh: 今曆推之，是歲三月癸亥朔，加時在晝，去交分二十六日五千九百十七分入食限，失閏也。

translations.literal: Calculated by the present calendar, in that year the guihai new moon of the third month, calculated moment in daytime, distance from crossing 26 days 5,917 parts entering eclipse limit—an intercalary month was missed.
translations.idiomatic: By the present calendar, the guihai new moon of the third month of that year occurred in daylight, with a nodal distance of 26 days and 5,917 parts within the eclipse limit—an intercalary month had been omitted.

sentences.zh: 文公十五年己酉歲，六月辛丑朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: Fifteenth year of Duke Wen, year jiyou: on the xinchou new moon of the sixth month, the sun was eclipsed.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year of Duke Wen (jiyou), on the xinchou new moon of the sixth month, there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 今曆推之，是歲六月辛丑朔，加時在晝，交分二十六日四千四百七十三分入食限。

translations.literal: Calculated by the present calendar, in that year the xinchou new moon of the sixth month, calculated moment in daytime, crossing distance 26 days 4,473 parts entering eclipse limit.
translations.idiomatic: By the present calendar, the xinchou new moon of the sixth month of that year occurred in daylight, with a nodal distance of 26 days and 4,473 parts within the eclipse limit.

sentences.zh: 宣公八年庚申歲，秋七月甲子，日有食之。

translations.literal: Eighth year of Duke Xuan, year gengshen: in the seventh month of autumn on jiazi, the sun was eclipsed.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Duke Xuan (gengshen), on jiazi in the seventh month of autumn, there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 杜預以七月甲子晦食。

translations.literal: Du Yu held it was an eclipse on the last day jiazi of the seventh month.
translations.idiomatic: Du Yu held that the eclipse fell on the last day of the seventh month, jiazi.

sentences.zh: 姜氏云：「十月甲子朔，食。

translations.literal: Master Jiang said: "The jiazi new moon of the tenth month—eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Ji said: "The jiazi new moon of the tenth month had the eclipse.

sentences.zh: 」《大衍》同。

translations.literal: " The Dayan Calendar agrees.

Calculated by the Shoushi Calendar, only the gengchen new moon of the tenth month in Duke Xiang's twenty-first year and the guisi new moon of the eighth month in his twenty-fourth year do not enter eclipse limit—since calendars have existed, there is no principle of two eclipses in the same month.

translations.idiomatic: The Shoushi Calendar is an exact match; the Daming Calendar is loose.

translations.literal: Of the forty-five cases above, of exact matches Shoushi eighteen, Daming eleven;
translations.idiomatic: Of the forty-five cases above, of exact matches the Shoushi Calendar has eighteen and the Daming Calendar eleven;

sentences.zh: 親者，《授時》十有八，《大明》十有七；

translations.idiomatic: of close matches the Shoushi Calendar has eighteen and the Daming Calendar seventeen;

sentences.zh: 疏者，《授時》無，《大明》二；

translations.idiomatic: of loose matches the Shoushi Calendar has none and the Daming Calendar two;

sentences.zh: 疏遠者，《授時》無，《大明》一。

translations.literal: Of distant matches, Shoushi none, Daming one.
translations.idiomatic: of distant matches the Shoushi Calendar has none and the Daming Calendar one.

sentences.zh: 日平行一度，月平行十三度十九分度之七，一晝夜之間，月先日十二度有奇，曆二十九日五十三刻，復追及日，與之同度，是謂經朔。

translations.literal: The sun's mean motion is one degree per day, the moon's mean motion thirteen degrees and seven parts of nineteen parts of a degree; within one day and night the moon leads the sun by somewhat more than twelve degrees; after twenty-nine days and fifty-three ke it again catches up to the sun and shares the same position—this is called mean new moon.
translations.idiomatic: The sun's mean motion is one degree per day and the moon's mean motion thirteen degrees and seven-nineteenths of a degree; in one day and night the moon outruns the sun by somewhat more than twelve degrees; after twenty-nine days and fifty-three ke it again overtakes the sun and shares the same position—this is called mean new moon.

sentences.zh: 經朔雲者，謂合朔大量不出此也。

translations.literal: "Mean new moon" means that the bulk of conjunctions fall within this reckoning.
translations.idiomatic: "Mean new moon" means that the bulk of conjunctions fall within this reckoning.

sentences.zh: 日有盈縮，月有遲疾，以盈縮遲疾之數損益之，始為定朔。

translations.literal: The sun has expansion and contraction, the moon has slowing and speeding; applying the numbers of expansion-contraction and fast-slow as additions and subtractions, one obtains true new moon.
translations.idiomatic: The sun has variation in speed and the moon has fast and slow motion; by adding and subtracting the correction numbers for solar variation and lunar anomaly, one obtains true new moon.

sentences.zh: 初曆法用平朔，止知一大一小，為法之不可易，初聞三大二小之說，皆不以為然。

translations.literal: At first calendrical methods used mean new moon, knowing only one large and one small month as the unalterable rule; when they first heard of the doctrine of three large and two small months, none regarded it as plausible.
translations.idiomatic: Early calendars used mean new moon, recognizing only the alternation of one large and one small month as an unalterable rule; when people first heard of three large and two small months in a sequence, none found it credible.

sentences.zh: 自有曆以來，下訖麟德，而定朔始行，四大三小，理數自然，唐人弗克若天，而止用平朔。

translations.literal: From the time calendars began down to the Linde era, true new moon was finally put into practice, with four large and three small months following naturally from the reckoning; the Tang people could not conform to Heaven and reverted to mean new moon alone.
translations.idiomatic: From the first calendars down to the Linde era, true new moon was finally adopted, with four large and three small months arising naturally from the reckoning; the Tang could not follow Heaven's pattern and reverted to mean new moon alone.

sentences.zh: 迨本朝至元，而常議方革。

translations.literal: By our dynasty's Zhiyuan era, the old practice was finally reformed.
translations.idiomatic: Only in our dynasty's Zhiyuan era was this longstanding practice finally reformed.

sentences.zh: 至如進朔之意，止欲避晦日月見，殊不思合朔在酉戌亥，距前日之卯十八九辰矣，若進一日，則晦不見月，此論誠然。

translations.literal: As for the intent of advancing the new moon, it was only to avoid seeing the moon on the last day of the month; they gave no thought to the fact that when conjunction falls in you, xu, or hai, it is already eighteen or nineteen chen from the mao of the previous day—if one advances a day, the last day would not show the moon. This argument is indeed valid.
translations.idiomatic: The purpose of advancing the new moon was merely to keep the moon from being visible on the last day of the month; they never considered that when conjunction falls in you, xu, or hai, it is already eighteen or nineteen double-hours past the mao of the previous day—advancing a day would indeed prevent the moon from appearing on the last day. This argument is sound.

sentences.zh: 茍合朔在辰申之間，法不當進，距前日之卯已逾十四五度，則月見於晦，庸得免乎？

translations.literal: If conjunction falls between chen and shen, the rule should not advance it; if it is already more than fourteen or fifteen degrees past the mao of the previous day, the moon will appear on the last day—how can that be avoided?
translations.idiomatic: If conjunction falls between chen and shen, the rule should not advance it; when it is already more than fourteen or fifteen degrees past the mao of the previous day, the moon will appear on the last day—how can that be avoided?

sentences.zh: 且月之隱見，本天道之自然，朔之進退，出人為之牽強，孰若廢人用天，不復虛進，為得其實哉。

translations.literal: Moreover, the moon's visibility and invisibility follow Heaven's natural course; advancing or delaying the new moon is a human contrivance—how much better to abandon human artifice for Heaven's way and no longer make empty advances, thereby obtaining the true reckoning?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the moon's visibility and invisibility follow Heaven's natural course, whereas advancing or delaying the new moon is a human contrivance—how much better to set aside human manipulation, follow Heaven, and make no empty advance, thereby obtaining the true reckoning?

sentences.zh: 至理所在，奚恤乎人言，可為知者道也。

translations.literal: Where ultimate principle lies, why worry about popular opinion? This may be told to those who understand.
translations.idiomatic: Where ultimate principle lies, why worry about popular opinion? This may be told to those who understand.

sentences.zh: 不用積年日法

translations.literal: Not Using Accumulated Years and Day Fraction
translations.idiomatic: Not Using Accumulated Years and Day Fraction

sentences.zh: 曆法之作，所以步日月之躔離，候氣朔之盈虛，不揆其端，無以測知天道，而與之吻合；

translations.literal: Calendars are made to track the sun and moon's courses and positions, and to observe the surplus and deficit of qi and new moon; without gauging the starting point, there is no way to measure and know the Way of Heaven and align with it;
translations.idiomatic: Calendars are made to track the courses and positions of the sun and moon and to observe the surplus and deficit of qi and new moon; without gauging the starting point, there is no way to measure the Way of Heaven and align with it;

sentences.zh: 然日月之行遲速不同，氣朔之運參差不一，昔人立法，必推求往古生數之始，謂之演紀上元。

translations.literal: Yet the sun and moon move at different speeds, and the cycles of qi and new moon vary unevenly; in making calendars, the ancients always traced back to the beginning of numerical generation in antiquity, calling this the ephemeris epoch or upper origin.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the sun and moon move at different speeds, and the cycles of qi and new moon vary unevenly; in making calendars, the ancients always traced back to the beginning of numerical generation in antiquity, calling this the ephemeris epoch or upper origin.

sentences.zh: 當斯之際，日月五星同度，如合璧連珠然。

translations.literal: At that moment, sun, moon, and the five planets shared the same position, like jade combined on a disc or pearls strung together.
translations.idiomatic: At that moment, sun, moon, and the five planets shared the same position, like jade combined on a disc or pearls strung together.

sentences.zh: 惟其世代綿遠，馴積其數至逾億萬，後人厭其布算繁多，互相推考，斷截其數而增損日法，以為得改憲之術，此歷代積年日法所以不能相同者也。

translations.literal: Because the ages stretch so far back and the numbers accumulate gradually to more than hundreds of millions, later people grew weary of the numerous computations; they consulted one another, truncated the numbers and adjusted the day fraction, thinking they had found the art of reforming the calendar—this is why accumulated years and day fractions could not be the same across dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: Because the ages stretch so far back and the numbers accumulate gradually to more than hundreds of millions, later people grew weary of the numerous computations; they consulted one another, truncated the numbers and adjusted the day fraction, thinking they had found the art of reforming the calendar—this is why accumulated years and day fractions could not be the same across dynasties.

sentences.zh: 然行之未遠，浸復差失，蓋天道自然，豈人為附會所能茍合哉？

translations.literal: Yet when put into practice it did not go far before errors gradually reappeared; the Way of Heaven is naturally so—how could forced human alignment achieve a fit?
translations.idiomatic: Yet when put into practice it did not go far before errors gradually reappeared; the Way of Heaven follows its own course—how could artificial forced alignment ever achieve a true fit?

sentences.zh: 夫七政運行於天，進退自有常度，茍原始要終，候驗周匝，則象數昭著，有不容隱者，又何必舍目前簡易之法，而求億萬年宏闊之術哉？

translations.literal: The seven luminaries move through heaven, advancing and retreating each with fixed regularity; if one traces from origin to completion and observes and verifies through a full cycle, the numerical correspondences become manifest and cannot be concealed—why then abandon the simple methods at hand and seek vast techniques spanning hundreds of millions of years?
translations.idiomatic: The seven luminaries move through the heavens, each advancing and retreating by fixed regular measure; if one traces matters from origin to completion and observes and verifies through a full cycle, the numerical correspondences stand forth plainly and cannot be hidden—why then abandon the simple methods at hand and pursue grand techniques spanning hundreds of millions of years?

sentences.zh: 今《授時曆》以至元辛巳為元，所用之數，一本諸天，秒而分，分而刻，刻而日，皆以百為率，比之他曆積年日法，推演附會，出於人為者，為得自然。

translations.literal: Now the Shoushi Calendar takes the xinsi year of Zhiyuan as its epoch; the numbers it employs all derive from heaven—seconds to minutes, minutes to ke, ke to days, all at the rate of one hundred—compared with other calendars' accumulated years and day fractions, which are deduced by forced alignment and derive from human artifice, it achieves what is natural.
translations.idiomatic: The Shoushi Calendar now takes the xinsi year of Zhiyuan as its epoch; the numbers it employs all derive from heaven—seconds to minutes, minutes to ke, and ke to days, all reckoned by hundreds—and compared with the accumulated years and day fractions of other calendars, which are worked out by forced alignment and human artifice, it attains what is natural.

sentences.zh: 或曰：「昔人謂建曆之本，必先立元，元正然後定日法，法定然後度周天以定分至，然則曆之有積年日法尚矣。

translations.literal: Some say: 'The ancients held that in establishing a calendar one must first set the epoch; once the epoch is fixed one then sets the day fraction; once the fraction is fixed one then measures the circuit of heaven to fix the equinoxes and solstices—thus calendars have always had accumulated years and day fractions.'
translations.idiomatic: Some say: 'The ancients held that in establishing a calendar one must first set the epoch; once the epoch is fixed one then determines the day fraction; once the fraction is fixed one then measures the circuit of heaven to fix the equinoxes and solstices—thus calendars have always relied on accumulated years and day fractions.'

sentences.zh: 自黃帝以來，諸曆轉相祖述，殆七八十家，未聞舍此而能成者。

translations.literal: From the Yellow Emperor onward, calendars have been passed down one after another, totaling some seventy or eighty schools; none are known to have succeeded by abandoning this.
translations.idiomatic: From the time of the Yellow Emperor, calendars have been handed down in succession, totaling some seventy or eighty schools, and none are known to have succeeded by abandoning this practice.

sentences.zh: 今一切削去，無乃昧於本原，而考求未得其方歟？

translations.literal: Now that all this has been entirely cut away, might one not be ignorant of the fundamental source and fail to find the right method of investigation?
translations.idiomatic: Now that all of this has been entirely cut away, might one not be ignorant of the fundamental source and fail to find the right method of inquiry?

sentences.zh: 」是殆不然。

translations.literal: 」This is probably not so.
translations.idiomatic: This is probably not so.

sentences.zh: 晉杜預有云：「治曆者，當順天以求合，非為合以驗天。

translations.literal: Du Yu of Jin said: 'In regulating calendars, one should follow heaven to seek alignment, not seek alignment to verify heaven.'
translations.idiomatic: Du Yu of Jin said: 'In regulating calendars, one should follow heaven to seek alignment, not seek alignment in order to verify heaven.'

sentences.zh: 」前代演積之法，不過為合驗天耳。

translations.literal: 」The methods of ephemeris computation in former ages were nothing more than aligning to verify heaven.
translations.idiomatic: The ephemeris computation methods of former ages were nothing more than aligning the calendar to verify heaven.

sentences.zh: 今以舊曆頗疏，乃命厘正，法之不密，在所必更，奚暇踵故習哉。

translations.literal: Now because the old calendar was rather loose, an order was issued to rectify it; where the method is insufficiently precise, change is inevitable—why would one have leisure to follow old habit?
translations.idiomatic: Because the old calendar was rather loose, an order was issued to rectify it; where the method is insufficiently precise, change is inevitable—why linger over old habits?

translations.literal: Therefore the accumulated years, day fractions, and years in use of every calendar since the Han are fully listed below, and the method of ephemeris computation is still appended, to resolve the doubts of those who question.
